records.summary: The South African Department of Basic Education is recruiting a Director: National School Nutrition Programme (NSNP) (DBE/66/2026) in Pretoria. The role leads national coordination, oversight and monitoring of the NSNP Conditional Grant, including policy, implementation of school feeding, nutrition education and sustainable food production, provincial support, reporting, risk management and stakeholder coordination. records.body_markdown:
## Overview

The South African Department of Basic Education is recruiting a Director: National School Nutrition Programme (NSNP) (DBE/66/2026) in Pretoria. The role leads national coordination, oversight and monitoring of the NSNP Conditional Grant, including policy, implementation of school feeding, nutrition education and sustainable food production, provincial support, reporting, risk management and stakeholder coordination. Salary is R1,317,384 per year. Applications close 5 October 2026.

## Location

Pretoria, South Africa

## Requirements

- NQF Level 7 qualification recognised by SAQA.
- Five years’ experience at middle/senior managerial level.
- In-depth experience in school nutrition, nutrition or food-security programming, conditional-grant management, or a comparable large-scale public-sector programme, with sound understanding of the National School Nutrition Programme.
- Experience in policy formulation and implementation and in managing diverse stakeholders and communities.
- Strong analytical, strategic, research, programme and project-management skills; knowledge of education-sector interfaces, nutrition/dietetics, and applicable public-service legislation and policies.
- Valid driver’s licence and willingness to travel extensively; strong computer literacy and ability to work collaboratively.

## How to apply

Submit the most recently approved Z83 Application for Employment Form (page 2 signed) and a detailed CV only. Indicate the post and reference DBE/66/2026. Apply by post to Private Bag X895, Pretoria, 0001; hand-deliver to the Department of Basic Education, 222 Struben Street, Pretoria; or email Sechele.O@dbe.gov.za, Segowa.M@dbe.gov.za, Kumalo.N@dbe.gov.za, or Skosana.th@dbe.gov.za. Certified supporting documents are requested from shortlisted candidates.

## Closing date

2026-10-05

## Official source

[Public Service Vacancy Circular 34 of 2026](https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/PUBLIC%20SERVICE%20VACANCY%20CIRCULAR%2034%20OF%202026.pdf)

records.title: Audit and Risk Committee Members (x5) (DBE/68/2026)
records.summary: The Department of Basic Education is recruiting five Audit and Risk Committee Members for a four-year renewable contract in the Office of the Director-General. Members will participate in committee deliberations, review internal controls and governance processes, oversee audit plans and outcomes, monitor audit recommendations, and review financial and performance reporting.
records.body_markdown:
## Overview

The Department of Basic Education is recruiting five Audit and Risk Committee Members for a four-year renewable contract in the Office of the Director-General. Members will participate in committee deliberations, review internal controls and governance processes, oversee audit plans and outcomes, monitor audit recommendations, and review financial and performance reporting.

## Location

Pretoria, South Africa

## Requirements

- NQF Level 6 qualification in Accounting, Auditing, Finance, Compliance, Business Management, Risk Management, IT or Law, recognised by SAQA.
- Committee Chairperson: minimum of 10 years of senior/executive management experience.
- Audit Committee Members: 5–10 years of senior/executive management experience.
- Combined committee experience in auditing, governance, risk management, information and communication technology, organisational performance management, performance information, external auditing or legal matters.
- Prior audit, risk or anti-fraud committee experience is strongly preferred.
- Competencies include independence, integrity, objectivity, reliability, knowledge of governance processes, risk-management principles and internal control, communication and leadership skills, and knowledge of the education sector.

## How to apply

Submit the most recently approved, fully completed and signed Z83 application form with a detailed CV only. Applications may be sent by post to Private Bag X895, Pretoria, 0001; hand-delivered to the Department of Basic Education, 222 Struben Street, Pretoria; or emailed to Sechele.O@dbe.gov.za, Segowa.M@dbe.gov.za, or Kumalo.N@dbe.gov.za. Indicate the post and reference number DBE/68/2026. The old Z83 form will result in disqualification.

## Closing date

2026-10-05

## Official source

[Public Service Vacancy Circular, Publication No. 34 of 2026](https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/PUBLIC%20SERVICE%20VACANCY%20CIRCULAR%2034%20OF%202026.pdf)

records.title: Deputy Director: Chief Information Security Officer (DBE/69/2026)
records.summary: The Department of Basic Education is recruiting a Deputy Director: Chief Information Security Officer in its Business Intelligence branch, Chief Directorate: Information and Management Systems, Directorate: Government Information Technology Office. The Level 12 post pays R1,101,468 per annum and covers cybersecurity governance, security controls, data protection, incident response, vulnerability management, third-party risk, disaster recovery and information-security training.
records.body_markdown:
## Overview

The Department of Basic Education is recruiting a Deputy Director: Chief Information Security Officer in its Business Intelligence branch, Chief Directorate: Information and Management Systems, Directorate: Government Information Technology Office. The Level 12 post pays R1,101,468 per annum and covers cybersecurity governance, security controls, data protection, incident response, vulnerability management, third-party risk, disaster recovery and information-security training.

## Location

Pretoria, South Africa

## Requirements

- NQF level 6 post-matric qualification in Information Technology, Information Systems or an equivalent qualification recognised by SAQA.
- Four years’ relevant experience as an Assistant Director or equivalent.
- At least two certifications from ITIL, COBIT, CISA, CISM, CISSP, CRISC or ISO 27001, plus at least five years’ experience as a Chief Information Security Officer or Information Security Officer.
- Experience managing networks and knowledge of enterprise/technology architecture, ICT systems and processes, Microsoft, virtualised and cloud environments, business continuity management, the E-government strategy and roadmap, data classification and vulnerability management.
- Valid driver’s licence.
- Applicants must use the most recently approved Z83 form, completed in full and signed on page 2, with a detailed CV; certified qualifications and other documents are requested from shortlisted candidates.

## How to apply

Submit the completed, signed latest Z83 form and detailed CV by post to Private Bag X895, Pretoria, 0001; hand-deliver to the Department of Basic Education, 222 Struben Street, Pretoria; or email the application to Sechele.O@dbe.gov.za, Segowa.M@dbe.gov.za, Kumalo.N@dbe.gov.za or Skosana.th@dbe.gov.za. Clearly state the post and reference DBE/69/2026. The notice says applicants should visit www.education.gov.za for departmental information.

The Department of Communications and Digital Technologies is recruiting a permanent Director: Technology Innovation and Artificial Intelligence Governance (ref. ## Overview

The Funza Lushaka Bursary Programme funds selected students pursuing teaching qualifications in identified priority subject areas. The programme covers tuition, accommodation or transport, meals, learning materials, a personal care allowance and teaching-practice support. South Africa

## Requirements

- First-time applicants must be 30 years or younger.
- Applicants must be South African citizens with a valid South African ID number.

Apply online through the e-Gov portal: register with personal information, log in, select Funza Lushaka Bursary Scheme, enter the OTP, accept the terms and conditions, select the 2027 application button, complete the required fields, and accept the declaration.

records.body_markdown:
## Overview

The Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment invites full-time South African students and Grade 12 learners who are not employed to apply for 2027 bursaries in environmental, biodiversity, conservation, chemicals and waste, climate and air quality, fisheries, forestry, oceans and coasts, and regulatory compliance fields. The bursary has a maximum value of R80,000. Successful recipients must sign a bursary contract and participate in the department’s internship programme after graduation.

## Location

South Africa (study at a recognised and accredited tertiary institution in South Africa; delivery addresses in Pretoria and Cape Town)

## Requirements

- South African citizen.
- Currently in Matric/Grade 12 or have completed Matric.
- Studying or intending to study full time in one of the listed fields.
- Enrolled or intending to enrol at a recognised and accredited tertiary institution in South Africa.
- Must not be employed or be an employee of DFFE.
- Must not have previously participated in the public service internship programme.
- Submit the prescribed application form with certified copies of the applicant’s and parent/guardian’s identity documents, qualifications/certificates and academic records, proof of registration or an admission/acceptance letter where applicable, parent/guardian income evidence, and any required affidavits; Honours/Master’s applicants must also provide a research proposal.
- Preference is given to previously disadvantaged candidates and persons living with disabilities.

## How to apply

Download and complete the official 2027 DFFE Bursary Application Form, clearly state the relevant reference number and qualification, and submit it by hand delivery or courier to the DFFE office in Pretoria or Cape Town, or by post to: The Director-General, Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, Private Bag X447, Pretoria, 0001, Attention: Learning and Development (Bursary Section). Faxed and emailed applications are not accepted; no late applications will be accepted.

## Overview

KPMG South Africa offers two bursary options for the 2027 academic year: a Pure Merit Bursary and a Merit Bursary with Financial Need. Applicants must first apply for a KPMG training contract, then submit the bursary application and required supporting documents online. Bursary recipients are required to enter a KPMG learnership/training contract after graduation.

## Location

South Africa

## Requirements

- Be a South African citizen.
- Have completed Matric and achieved at least four A symbols excluding Life Orientation.
- Study full-time toward a SAICA-accredited/recognised Chartered Accounting or CA(SA) qualification at a SAICA-accredited university.
- Complete the degree in the minimum number of years.
- Meet the academic thresholds: First Year—65% overall average and 70% Accounting; Second Year—65% overall average and 65% Accounting; Third Year—60% overall average and 60% Accounting; Honours/CTA—50% overall average and 55% Accounting.
- For the Merit Bursary with Financial Need, demonstrate financial need.

First apply for a KPMG training contract at https://kpmgza.taleo.net/careersection/kpmg_graduate/jobsearch.ftl?lang=en&portal=10205020166# and obtain the Taleo reference number. Then apply for the 2027 bursary at https://kpmg-students.readyplatform.co.za/Register using that reference number, and upload the required documents: certified ID, certified Matric certificate, latest academic record/transcripts, proof of university registration, updated fee statement and CV. ## Overview

## Location

South Africa

## Requirements

- South African citizen and resident in South Africa for at least three years before applying
- Currently in Matric and holding a Further Education & Training Certificate (General) or recognised equivalent

records.body_markdown:
## Overview

UNISA describes its 2027 SETA bursary as invite-based and tied to academic performance and qualification. Eligible students receive invitations through their myLife email; students not invited may apply directly to the relevant participating SETA. Listed SETAs cover finance and accounting, construction, logistics/transport, safety and security, education, banking and broader services-related qualifications or skills development.

## Location

South Africa

## Requirements

- South African citizen aged 18 to 35 years
- Currently unemployed; SASSETA and Services SETA bursaries also fund employed students
- At least a 50% average in the prior academic year of study, where applicable to the particular SETA bursary
- Academic performance and qualification must meet the relevant invite-based and SETA-specific criteria
- Qualification must align with the relevant SETA's stated area, where applicable

## How to apply

UNISA-eligible students should check their myLife email for the bursary invitation. Students who are not invited must apply directly to the relevant SETA; UNISA does not administer those applications. The UNISA page links to FASSET (http://www.fasset.org.za/), CETA (http://www.ceta.org.za/), TETA (http://www.teta.org.za/), SASSETA (http://www.sasseta.org.za/), ETDP-SETA (http://www.etdpseta.org.za/), BANK SETA (http://www.bankseta.org.za/) and Services SETA (http://www.serviceseta.org.za/). For information, UNISA lists Mrs Ndlovu at Ndlovmj2@unisa.ac.za.

## Closing date

Not stated on the source page — verify before publishing.

## Official source

[SETA bursaries](https://www.unisa.ac.za/sites/myunisa/default/Student-Affairs-&-SRC/Student-funding:-bursaries-&-loans/Undergraduate-Bursaries/SETA-bursaries)

> Verified on 2026-10-01. Always confirm the closing date and application instructions on the official source before publishing or applying.
